en.headline: Lee says crackdown on poor subdivided flats will not leave tenants homeless
en.dek: On RTHK’s Saturday Accountability, the chief executive said the government would not use extreme or high-handed means and cited a 65 percent registration rate under the Basic Housing Unit regime.
body: Chief Executive John Lee said the government would not use extreme or high-handed methods when it moves to stamp out substandard subdivided flats, and would not leave tenants without a roof over their heads.

Speaking on RTHK’s Saturday Accountability programme, Lee said the first five-year plan set a target of basically resolving poor-quality subdivided units inside residential buildings by 2030, while pressing ahead with the Basic Housing Unit regime. He said cases would be handled according to procedure and with tenants’ needs in mind.

Asked whether operators might push units underground, Lee said the Basic Housing Unit ordinance includes a registration system and that the current registration rate had reached 65 percent. He said he believed most operators wanted to run legally.

The government would also sample-check registered units, he said, and existing public complaint channels made it easier for the authorities to identify non-compliant flats. He expressed confidence that the work could proceed on the planned timetable.

zh.headline: 李家超：取締劣質劌房不會用高壓手段
zh.dek: 特首在港台《星期六問責》表示，不會因取締劣質劌房而令住戶無瓦遮頭，簡樸房登記率現達65%。
body: 行政長官李家超表示，政府取締劣質劌房時不會採用極端和高壓手段，亦不會令住戶「無瓦遮頭」。
他出席香港電台節目《星期六問責》時說，香港第一個五年規劃提出有序取締劣質劌房，目標在2030年內基本解決住宅大廈內的劣質劌房問題，並全力推展簡樸房制度。他強調會按程序處理，並考慮住戶需要。
被問到劣質劌房會否轉入地下，李家超說簡樸房條例設有登記制度，現時登記率達到65%，他相信絕大部分經營者都希望在合法情況下經營。
他表示，政府會抽樣審查已登記的簡樸房，加上坊間有不少投訴平台，當局較容易掌握哪些單位屬於違規劣質劌房，相信整體可按時間表有序推進。
